mechanisms.behavior: Four balls queue below the apron at optos 32–35. Coil 2 sends the leading ball through eject opto 31 into the shooter lane. Retained bsTrough initializes switches 32–35 and pulses switch 31 on release. Draining replenishes the queue. Occupancy follows actual balls, not the drain kicker. Boot with the physical queue populated; a jam at the release obstructs launch.
mechanisms.label: Four-ball Trough

mechanisms.behavior: Coil 1 launches the ball waiting at shooter switch 18. Retained FireCatapult/bsCatapult supplies the launch and releases switch 18 as the ball leaves. Hidden CatapultKicker and CatapultLaunchKicker are separate staging/motion helpers, not interchangeable factory sensor locations. A trapped ball keeps switch 18 occupied.
mechanisms.label: Shooter / Catapult

mechanisms.behavior: The left cup closes switch 37 on capture. Coil 5 ejects the ball and switch 37 releases after departure. The retained ball stack owns capture/release. A failed kick leaves occupancy, rather than pulsing a trough input.
mechanisms.label: Left Corner Eject

mechanisms.behavior: Ball closes switch 28 in the left rear cup. Coil 14 fires the vertical up-kicker to the rope feed route; switch 28 releases after departure. Retained VUK1..VUKTop transport helpers and timer are one physical ball path, not extra solenoids. A blocked tube can leave switch 28 occupied.
mechanisms.label: Left Rear Popper

mechanisms.behavior: One dual-winding scoop has power coil 3/hold coil 9. Initially raised with 61 active, the retained hold callback moves it and writes switch 61. Beam 42 behind the scoop and made-jab beam 36 report balls separately. Lowering opens the jab route; raising catches/deflects. Restore raised state at startup and let a jam prevent the position transition.
mechanisms.label: Left Jab Scoop

mechanisms.behavior: One scoop uses power coil 4/hold coil 10 and starts raised with 62 active. Retained hold callback moves it. Beam 43 behind the scoop and made-jab beam 38 are ball sensors; switch 38 is an unmasked ROM-active public 0 exception. Lowering opens the route, distinct from ball beam events.
mechanisms.label: Right Jab Scoop

mechanisms.behavior: Motor 27 rotates a shared pole carrying boxer and heavy-bag faces; control 26 reverses direction. A-22260 optos 41/46/47/48 encode facing marks. Impacts 12/66/67/68 are separate target contacts. Coils 11 (right) and 13 (left) lift spring-return arms. Retained model wraps ±180, advances 1 degree per 15 ms, and opens switch 41 near 0, 46 near ±180, 47 near -27.5, 48 near +27.5. These windows/speed are simulation clues, not measured cams. Boot must answer ROM motor commands with changing feedback; static marks can stall self-test. A jam is distinct from an impact.

mechanisms.behavior: Motor 25 turns a continuous rope; switch 64 senses its cam. Magnet 7 catches the ball at 45, and coil 33 pops it for the rope to pass underneath. Switch 78 is entry, switch 71 is the downstream exit. T.16 home points downward at 45 degrees with CAM OPEN; ball opto indication is OPEN with a ball on the magnet. Retained 720 step circle asserts switch 64 at phase 0..20/700..720 and kicks in a difficulty-dependent window. These are table settings, not RPM. Model missed catches, departure, motor coast and real sensor travel.
mechanisms.label: Jump Rope

mechanisms.behavior: Separate coils 35 (left) and 36 (right) drive fists against the bag. Switch 72 is ball entry; switch 65 (SW-1A-215) senses motion/impact. Retained fists spring back and a bag timer pulses switch 65. Factory Power/Hold type labels do not make the two AE-27-1200 coils one dual-winding flipper. Default both retracted; a failed stroke can leave switch 65 quiet.
mechanisms.label: Speed Bag and Fists

mechanisms.behavior: One post uses power coil 6/hold coil 12. Retained hold callback raises it and writes switch 75=1, lowering to switch 75=0 on release. Default down; preserve position if jammed. Lamp 85 is its separate illumination circuit, not its actuator.
mechanisms.label: Center Up/Down Post

mechanisms.behavior: Coil 8 moves a spring-return factory post in the right route. Switch 73 senses a ball in the danger-zone area, not post position. Retained DangerZoneMod=1 substitutes a gate; the factory recreation must restore the post. The gate geometry is an aftermarket overlay.
mechanisms.label: Danger Zone Post Diverter

mechanisms.behavior: Coil 28 lowers the retention pin and releases balls. Spring return raises it. Three right-upper channel contacts 15/57/58 sense balls; switch 74 is entry. Retained timer delays pin return after release, a transport clue rather than measured factory timing. A jam can leave balls captured after the command.
mechanisms.label: Lock Pin / Three-ball Lock

mechanisms.behavior: Coil 34 changes the upper ramp fork. Switches 44 (entry), 11 (made ramp) and 76 (top of ramp) are ball sensors, not home contacts. Retained default closed; energizing raises the model and collision posts. Spring return restores closed. This is distinct from the danger-zone post.
mechanisms.label: Upper Ramp Diverter

mechanisms.behavior: Ball deflects left rubber, scoring switch 51 closes, and ROM coil 15 kicks it. Assembly has separate A-17800 kick and diode-equipped A-17794 scoring contacts. Animation returns to rest; a stuck contact is a fault.
mechanisms.label: Left Slingshot

mechanisms.behavior: Ball deflects right rubber and scoring switch 52; ROM coil 16 supplies rebound. A-17800 kick and A-17794 scoring contacts are separate. Retained animation springs back to rest.
mechanisms.label: Right Slingshot

mechanisms.behavior: Single FL-15411 dual-winding flipper has power coil 45/hold coil 46, remapped from printed 29/30. Button opto 112 and EOS 111 are distinct. Retained hold callback animates motion; power delivers the stroke and hold maintains it. Spring return restores rest. No upper flipper is fitted.
mechanisms.label: Lower Right Flipper

mechanisms.behavior: Single FL-15411 flipper has power coil 47/hold coil 48, printed 31/32. Button 114 and EOS 113 are distinct. Power gives stroke, hold maintains it, and spring return restores rest. Upper virtual 118 can reach ROM flipper control without a physical upper coil.
mechanisms.label: Lower Left Flipper
